result: During myogenesis, caspase-3 selectively degrades four peripheral Nups (Nup358, Nup214, Nup153, Tpr) and one transmembrane Nup (Pom121) in a reversible manner, while scaffold Nups (Nup96, Nup93) remain intact. This selective proteolysis is termed 'NPC trimming' and differs from the complete NPC destruction seen in apoptosis.
evaluation: All three reviewers explicitly praise the work and methodology. Reviewer 1 states the methodology is 'convincing and state-of-the-art,' Reviewer 2 describes the work as 'elegant and interesting' performed at 'superb quality,' and Reviewer 3 notes 'the data are of high quality and are well presented' with 'an interesting mechanism demonstrated whereby nuclear and cytosolically-oriented nups are specifically degraded from the NPC.'

result: Trimmed NPCs become nuclear export-defective while maintaining nuclear import and passive permeability barrier function. This is demonstrated by increased nuclear-to-total mRNA ratio (from 34% to 60%), decreased cytoplasmic-to-nuclear ratio of NES-GFP reporters, and nuclear exclusion of large dextrans.
evaluation: Reviewer 3 specifically highlights this as a key finding, stating there is 'a specific inhibition of nuclear export' while 'nuclear import and passive permeability barrier remain mostly functional.' The reviewers raise no concerns about these functional characterizations of trimmed NPCs.

result: NPC trimming leads to nuclear accumulation of diverse protein classes including focal adhesion proteins (FAK, Hic-5, zyxin, paxillin), tubulins, Annexin proteins, and mitochondrial enzymes. Quantitative mass spectrometry identified ~236 proteins that increased >fourfold in nuclear soluble fraction, and caspase inhibition prevented most of these changes.
evaluation: Reviewer 3 specifically praises this work, stating 'A highlight is a quantitative proteomic analysis of nuclear fractions that nicely demonstrates the change in the nuclear proteome upon NPC trimming, which includes elevated levels of many NES-containing factors. An important control is that these nuclear proteome changes don't occur when caspases are inhibited.' This represents strong explicit support for the proteomics findings.

result: NPC trimming by non-apoptotic caspases was observed in neurogenesis, with survivin downregulation and concomitant activation of caspase-3 and proteolysis of Nup153 and PARP during neural precursor cell differentiation.
evaluation: Reviewer 3 notes the work demonstrates NPC trimming 'as a key element of muscle (and other) differentiation programs,' implicitly accepting the neurogenesis data. No reviewer raises concerns about the neuronal differentiation experiments.

result: NPC trimming was observed during ER stress induced by tunicamycin treatment, with similar selective degradation of peripheral Nups while scaffold Nups remained protected. Chronic ER stress forces prolonged NPC trimming before apoptosis is triggered.
evaluation: The reviewers accept the ER stress data as part of the broader demonstration of NPC trimming in different contexts. Reviewer 3 acknowledges the work shows NPC trimming 'as a key element of muscle (and other) differentiation programs,' which would encompass the stress response findings. No specific concerns are raised about the ER stress experiments.

result: NPC trimming is reversible because the NPC core scaffold remains intact, allowing functional NPCs to be quickly restored once caspases are quenched. This reversibility distinguishes NPC trimming from irreversible apoptotic NPC destruction.
evaluation: Reviewer 1 explicitly notes the work 'uncovers that caspases can achieve high substrate specificity during differentiation,' which supports the selective/reversible nature of the process. Reviewer 3 states there is 'a new broadly impactful concept being introduced - that caspases need not be destructive but they can be productively utilized to contribute to cell fate decisions,' directly supporting the reversibility concept.

result: NPC trimming explains how FAK becomes transiently nuclear during myogenesis. Nuclear FAK removes MBD2 from the Myog promoter to de-repress myogenin expression, and loss of MBD2-genome binding occurs within 24 hr as FAK accumulates in the nucleus.
evaluation: The reviewers do not specifically critique the FAK-myogenin mechanistic connection. Reviewer 2 notes the authors 'suggest mechanistic insights into exactly why this limited proteolysis is needed for myogenesis,' implicitly accepting the proposed mechanisms including the FAK pathway.

result: Active caspase-3, -9, and -12 were detected in differentiating C2C12 cells, with caspase activity peaking at 16-24 hr and being quenched by 32-60 hr. Survivin downregulation precedes caspase-3 activation, and active caspase-3 arises before myogenin upregulation.
evaluation: The reviewers accept the temporal characterization of caspase activation. Reviewer 2 notes the work shows 'the NPC-related course of events during cellular differentiation,' implicitly accepting the timing data. No concerns are raised about the caspase activation kinetics.

result: The behavior of caspase-generated Nup fragments differs between differentiation and apoptosis. In differentiating cells, Tpr C-terminal fragment dissociates partially (only 5-10% complete dissociation), and Pom121 pore-side domain does not fully dissociate, showing heterogeneity in fragment behavior.
evaluation: Reviewer 3 notes 'fragments are sometimes associated with the NPCs,' acknowledging the partial dissociation phenotype. The detailed characterization of fragment behavior is not challenged by any reviewer.

result: Trimmed NPCs in differentiating cells retain normal Crm1 localization and do not cluster, distinguishing them from apoptotic NPCs. Importin localization is also unaffected by NPC trimming.
evaluation: These observations support the distinction between NPC trimming and apoptosis, which reviewers accept. Reviewer 3's statement that 'nuclear import and passive permeability barrier remain mostly functional' is consistent with these findings.

result: Both TprC⁻ Myog⁻ and TprC⁻ Myog⁺ cell states were identified in differentiating C2C12 cells and primary myoblasts. The presence of TprC⁻ Myog⁺ cells demonstrates that nuclear import remains functional even when NPCs are trimmed.
evaluation: This finding supports the functional characterization of trimmed NPCs. Reviewer 3's acceptance that 'nuclear import...remain[s] mostly functional' is consistent with these observations. No reviewer challenges this data.

result: Calpain inhibition delayed but did not prevent caspase-3/12 activation and peripheral Nup degradation, suggesting calpains participate in caspase activation but are not responsible for NPC trimming itself.
evaluation: This mechanistic detail about the caspase activation pathway is not questioned by reviewers. It supports the conclusion that caspases, not calpains, are directly responsible for NPC trimming.

result: Leptomycin B (Crm1 inhibitor) enhances myogenin expression when added to differentiation medium, while Q-VD-OPh (pan-caspase inhibitor) significantly suppresses myogenin upregulation, cell-cell fusion, and myosin heavy chain expression.
evaluation: These pharmacological experiments support the functional importance of NPC trimming for myogenesis. Reviewer 2 notes the authors provide 'mechanistic insights into exactly why this limited proteolysis is needed for myogenesis,' which these experiments help establish.

result: NPC trimming may be a general feature of cell differentiation and represents a new paradigm for caspase function. The authors suggest it is time to reassess the death-centric view of caspases, as apoptotic NPC destruction may be an extreme version of NPC trimming.
evaluation: Reviewer 1 explicitly states this work 'uncovers that caspases can achieve high substrate specificity during differentiation' and will be 'of broad interest to cell biologists.' Reviewer 3 emphasizes 'there is a new broadly impactful concept being introduced - that caspases need not be destructive but they can be productively utilized to contribute to cell fate decisions.' This represents strong support for the conceptual advance.

result: NPC trimming plays a key role in shaping the nuclear proteome during myogenesis, revealing the importance of protein translocation in cell differentiation. The nuclear proteome changes dramatically and rapidly in response to myogenic signals.
evaluation: While Reviewer 3 praises the proteomic data as 'valuable,' they note the work 'fall[s] short in demonstrating that NPC trimming is actually required for the execution of the differentiation program.' This indicates the causal role of NPC trimming in differentiation, while supported by correlative evidence, lacks definitive proof of requirement.
